description:
Nepal is observing a day of national mourning for the victims of the flood disaster, with more than 1,300 people dead and thousands still missing. Climate policy specialist Abhishek Shrestha told Al Jazeera the disaster is “undoubtedly” linked to climate change, citing the IPCC's findings on Himalayan glacier recession. He said there are 47 potential glacial lakes in the Himalayan range that pose a threat of bursting, warning that “there is much likelihood this kind of incident might happen in coming years.” He called the event “an alarming bell” for better preparedness. Shrestha said Nepal needs unconditional recovery funds to avoid a further debt burden and stressed the need to “put mountain as one of the agenda items into the COP discussion”, adding that “for us, this climate change is about survival.” He also called for rethinking hydropower infrastructure and settlements near floodplains.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Search and rescue efforts continue in Nepal, 11 days after a flash flood swept through the Himalayan region.
Authorities say thousands of people are in temporary shelters, and the true scale of the human cost is still emerging.

Mona Sherpa, Country Director for CARE Nepal, says survivors urgently need food, shelter and healthcare, while the authorities must ensure they do not return to areas still at risk of further flooding and landslides.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Jamaica is taking a new step in its campaign for reparations over Britain’s role in slavery, this time, using the law.
A government delegation is in London seeking answers on whether the enslavement of Jamaicans was unlawful and whether Britain now has a duty to provide redress.

Al Jazeera’s Sonia Gallego reports from London.
